title: What should I ask Yiyang Zhuge (诸葛一杨), also known as Zhong Shu (仲树)? - Marginal REVOLUTION
gist: Tyler Cowen previews a Conversation with Yiyang Zhuge (Zhong Shu), a China-based political theorist, translator of Hannah Arendt and Plutarch into Chinese, and host of the most popular Mandarin political-philosophy podcast, with 1m-plus subscribers.

insights.claim: Yiyang Zhuge hosts 'Monologues of a Committed Observer,' described as the most popular Mandarin political-philosophy podcast, with over one million subscribers.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: Illustrates the scale of demand for Western political-philosophy content among Chinese audiences via a single creator.
insights.quote: the most popular Mandarin political philosophy podcast “Monologues of a Committed Observer” with 1m+ subscribers
insights.locator: She hosts the most popular Mandarin political philosophy podcast

insights.claim: Zhuge is a major translator of Hannah Arendt into Chinese, having rendered The Human Condition, Life of the Mind, Men in Dark Times, and Rahel Varnhagen, plus the first Greek-to-Chinese translation of Plutarch's Moralia, a 2025 best-seller.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: Shows a channel through which Western canonical political thought is entering Chinese intellectual life.
insights.quote: Yiyang published the first Greek-to-Chinese translation of Plutarch’s Moralia, a best-selling philosophy book in 2025.
insights.locator: Yiyang published the first Greek-to-Chinese translation

insights.claim: Zhuge reports monthly on American higher education for Caixin Weekly, is a commentator on Hong Kong's Phoenix TV, and runs Princeton University Press's Political Philosophy Book Club for Chinese audiences.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: Maps the institutional footholds a single Chinese public intellectual occupies bridging US academia and Chinese media.
insights.locator: She reports on American higher ed monthly at print magazine Caixin Weekly
